prose:
Cory Doctorow uses a Mississippi campaign advertisement and the economics of substitution to argue that quantitative policy models can erase important differences in lived experience. The essay criticizes treating people’s needs as interchangeable inputs to austerity calculations.

This entry covers the opening argument of a wider political essay. Its policy judgments are the author’s, and the presence of AI-related terms elsewhere in the feed does not turn the piece into an empirical evaluation of model performance or establish every cited historical claim.
highlights: Essay critiques substitution as a policy shortcut
Campaign example illustrates its political argument
This is commentary, not an AI benchmark
Only the examined portion is summarized
